source: operator, 2026-10-17 ('Document and research first and make sure it can scale to large fleet number in parallel'; 'prioritize them with high prioritization')
title: Design set for a wave orchestrator that scales to a large parallel fleet
summary: The five wave-orchestrator items need one design before code. An audit on 2026-10-17 found: no wave-level supervisor (fleet.Supervisor is fire-and-wait, no CycleTimeout on the wave path), width bound by plan supply (the wave seed is the previous triage with top_n=1, widened only by inbox cards with files), PartitionGraph and PrefixQueue unwired, quota read once before the wave, and RunPool behind a non-default setting with a nil onTransition hook.
fix: Write docs/research/wave-orchestrator-2026-10.md (live online research on fleet scheduling, partitioning and merge queues), docs/plans/wave-orchestrator-2026-10.md with at least three approaches scored, an ADR and docs/architecture/wave-orchestrator.md, all through the docs-write skill. The design must state how it scales from 4 lanes to a large fleet (N far above 4): admission, partitioning, oversight cost per lane, quota and landing order.
acceptance: The four files exist and `evolve docs ste-lint --strict --changed origin/main --added` reports 0 findings.
The plan scores at least three approaches and names the winner and the strengths of each alternative.
The spec gives the cost of each orchestrator step as a function of the lane count N, and names the limit of N with its cause.
